tagline: The heart of Andalusia dazzles with the Real Alcázar, a vast Gothic cathedral, the sweeping Plaza de España and flamenco that was born in its streets.
overview: Seville, the capital of Andalusia, grew rich as Spain's monopoly port for trade with the Americas in the 1500s and 1600s. Its cathedral, built on the site of a mosque, is the largest Gothic cathedral in the world, and its bell tower, the Giralda, began life as a minaret.

Next door, the Real Alcázar is a royal palace still used by the Spanish royal family, with Mudéjar courtyards, tiled halls and gardens; together with the cathedral and the Archivo de Indias it is a UNESCO site. The Plaza de España, built for the 1929 expo, curves around a canal with tiled alcoves for every Spanish province.

Seville is the home of flamenco, sevillanas and tapas culture. The Santa Cruz and Triana neighbourhoods are full of tiled courtyards and bars, and spring brings Semana Santa processions and the April Fair. The Metropol Parasol, a giant wooden canopy, gives rooftop views.

funFacts.title: BIGGEST GOTHIC CATHEDRAL
funFacts.text: Seville Cathedral is the largest Gothic cathedral in the world.

funFacts.title: A MINARET TURNED BELL TOWER
funFacts.text: The Giralda was the minaret of the city's 12th-century mosque.

funFacts.title: A ROYAL PALACE STILL IN USE
funFacts.text: The Real Alcázar's upper floors are used by the Spanish royal family.

funFacts.title: COLUMBUS RESTS HERE
funFacts.text: A tomb in the cathedral holds remains attributed to Christopher Columbus.

funFacts.title: GATEWAY TO THE AMERICAS
funFacts.text: Seville held Spain's trade monopoly with the Americas for nearly two centuries.

funFacts.title: FILM LOCATION
funFacts.text: The Alcázar was used to film Game of Thrones scenes.

funFacts.title: WOODEN MUSHROOMS
funFacts.text: The Metropol Parasol is one of the world's largest wooden structures.

funFacts.title: BIRTHPLACE OF FLAMENCO
funFacts.text: Seville and its Triana district are central to flamenco's history.

funFacts.title: ORANGE TREES
funFacts.text: Seville's streets are lined with thousands of bitter orange trees.

funFacts.title: A SPRING FAIR
funFacts.text: The Feria de Abril fills the city with music and casetas each spring.
